Numbers manipulation vs maintenance is a group-level, task-evoked voxelwise contrast isolating active problem solving (arithmetic manipulation) vs an appropriate control; it reflects domain-general executive manipulation processes (ACC/IFG/caudate) as well as number-specific processing.
Contrast directly probes active mathematical computation (addition of four two-digit numbers) vs maintenance, i.e., isolates mathematical problem solving.

Numbers manipulation engages language-mediated processes (left IFG/ITG; participants reported phonological strategies); the contrast isolates manipulation vs maintenance and thus verbal problem-solving components are present.

Numbers manipulation also recruits right fronto-parietal and bilateral IPS regions overlapping with spatial manipulation (mirror/mental workspace), indicating visuospatial problem-solving components during arithmetic manipulation.
Task is numerical/arithmetic manipulation rather than formal logical inference; does not meet LOGICAL_REASONING_I1 (no rule-based logical inference), so excluded.
Syllables manipulation vs maintenance is a group-level task contrast isolating active manipulation (word generation) vs control, engaging executive WM processes (ACC/IFG).

Syllables manipulation explicitly involves language-based manipulation and retrieval (generating a word from syllables) vs maintenance, isolating verbal problem-solving processes (left IFG/ITG).
Although some participants used visual strategies, the contrast targets language-based syllable manipulation rather than primary spatial reasoning; missing VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Syllable reordering/word generation is not formal logical inference; does not meet LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.
Locations manipulation vs maintenance is a group-level task contrast isolating active spatial manipulation (mirror transformation) vs control, engaging executive WM processes.

Contrast isolates active spatial manipulation (mirror-reversal of locations) vs maintenance and shows right fronto-parietal activations consistent with visuospatial problem solving.
Task is spatial manipulation rather than formal logical inference; does not meet LOGICAL_REASONING_I1.

Conjunction of manipulation vs maintenance across numbers, syllables, and locations identifies an executive/manipulation network (ACC/IFG orb/caudate) common to all materials, isolating domain-general problem-solving processes.

Conjunction isolates processes common across verbal, numeric, and spatial tasks (executive), not specifically language-based reasoning; missing VERBAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.
Conjunction targets domain-general executive network rather than spatial-specific manipulation; missing VISUOSPATIAL_PROBLEM_SOLVING_I1.

This study reports group-level, voxelwise fMRI analyses (whole-brain voxel ANOVA) of an active problem-solving task (simplified Sudoku) comparing task conditions (one-step vs two-step; simple vs complex). Stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) are reported. The contrast isolates problem-solving/goal-directed cognition independent of a single representational domain.

The task is a heuristic Sudoku puzzle emphasizing rule application and visuospatial configuration rather than active mathematical computation; it does not meet local inclusion for mathematical problem solving.
The task does not involve language-based reasoning or verbal problem solving; it fails the verbal local inclusion criteria.

Sudoku requires spatial/configurational reasoning over a grid (checking rows, columns, boxes) and the reported contrasts isolate these visuospatial problem-solving operations in a task-based, voxelwise analysis with stereotactic reporting.

The task requires rule-based inference and application of explicit heuristics (if-then rules) to determine the target digit, which constitutes logical/rule-based reasoning; the contrasts isolate these processes in a voxelwise task analysis with stereotactic reporting.

This analysis is from the same study reporting group-level, voxelwise fMRI contrasts of an active problem-solving task (simplified Sudoku) with valid condition comparisons and stereotactic (Talairach) reporting; it isolates domain-general problem-solving processes.
The task emphasizes heuristic rule application over numerical computation, so it does not meet the local inclusion criteria for mathematical problem solving.
The paradigm does not engage language-based reasoning as the primary process; it fails verbal local inclusion.

The simplified Sudoku requires spatial/configurational reasoning (rows/columns/boxes) and the analysis isolates these visuospatial problem-solving processes in a voxelwise task contrast with stereotactic reporting.

Participants apply explicit heuristic rules (if-then) to infer missing digits, meeting local criteria for logical/rule-based reasoning; the contrasts isolate this within task-based voxelwise analyses with stereotactic coordinates.

The contrast is a domain-specific comparison (logic vs math) rather than an analysis isolating domain-general problem solving processes versus a low-level/control baseline, so it does not meet the local inclusion requirement for domain-general problem solving.

The Type-of-problem contrast directly compares mathematical calculation trials to logical reasoning trials, isolating mathematical problem solving processes (math > logic). The analysis is a group-level voxelwise task contrast of problem solving with a valid comparator.

The Type-of-problem contrast isolates language-based reasoning (logic > math) with reported activation in perisylvian language areas (Broca's/Wernicke's), meeting group-level voxelwise and task-based criteria.

The contrast reveals right frontal and inferior parietal activations interpreted as construction/manipulation of mental models (visuospatial representations) for logic versus math, satisfying voxelwise task criteria and isolating visuospatial reasoning processes.

The contrast directly compares logical reasoning to mathematical calculation, isolating logical inference processes (logic > math) with reported right-frontal and language-related activations during reasoning.

The Level-of-difficulty main effect (hard > easy) reflects modulation of problem-solving demand across tasks and thus isolates domain-general increases in problem-solving/executive processing; analysis is a group-level voxelwise task contrast with valid comparator (hard vs easy).

The main effect of difficulty is not specific to mathematical computation (it pools across logic and math) and does not isolate mathematical problem solving versus a valid non-math control, so it fails the local inclusion requirement for math.
The difficulty main effect is not specific to language-based reasoning and does not isolate verbal problem solving versus an appropriate control, so it fails the local verbal inclusion criterion.

The main effect of difficulty is a domain-general contrast (hard vs easy across both tasks) and does not specifically isolate visuospatial reasoning processes versus a valid control, so it does not meet the visuospatial inclusion criterion.
The difficulty main effect pools across task types and does not specifically isolate logical inference independent of other domains, so it fails the logical reasoning inclusion requirement.

The Type × Difficulty interaction identifies regions selectively engaged for hard vs easy logic (e.g., right frontopolar BA10) and thus reflects domain-specific modulation rather than domain-general problem solving; it does not meet the domain-general inclusion criterion.

The interaction effect shows selective engagement for harder logical problems and reports no analogous math-specific difficulty modulation; it does not isolate mathematical problem solving, so it fails the math inclusion criterion.

The interaction highlights right frontopolar recruitment for complex logic; language areas were not reported as showing the interaction, so this analysis does not isolate verbal problem solving and fails the local verbal inclusion criterion.

Although the interaction pertains to complex model manipulation in logic, the reported region (right BA10/frontopolar) was interpreted as higher-order relational integration rather than a pure visuospatial subsystem; the interaction is task- and logic-specific rather than a clean visuospatial vs control contrast, so the visuospatial inclusion criterion is not met.

The Type × Difficulty interaction isolates regions (right frontopolar BA10) selectively engaged by harder logical (deductive) problems (hard logic > easy logic) and thus isolates logical inference processes; the analysis is a group-level voxelwise task contrast with valid comparator.
